SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.4
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the classic Raman pattern of a mono-substituted benzene: very strong ring-breathing band at 1005 cm⁻¹, another strong band at 1032 cm⁻¹, the C–H out-of-plane bend at 771 cm⁻¹ and ring C=C stretches at 1585–1606 cm⁻¹, plus the aromatic C–H stretch at 3064 cm⁻¹.  Aliphatic C–H stretches appear at 2879–2972 cm⁻¹ and the CH₃/CH₂ deformation at 1446 cm⁻¹, indicating an alkyl substituent but no OH (∼3400 cm⁻¹) or NH (∼3300 cm⁻¹) bands.  
Among the mono-alkyl benzene candidates (1, 5, 7), the spectrum best matches ethylbenzene (1: CCc1ccccc1).  Its reported Raman bands (≈1000, 1030, 1178–1205, 1450, 1605 cm⁻¹; 2880–2970 and 3060 cm⁻¹) coincide closely with the observed peaks.  Longer or halogenated side chains (5, 7) usually give additional distinctive low-frequency modes or C–Br stretches (∼600 cm⁻¹) not clearly present.  Therefore candidate 1 is the most consistent with the experimental data.
